title: Controlplane tactics braindump — 2026-07-29
content:
Purpose: quick capture from today’s mid-week sync + adhoc follow-ups. This is a working braindump — messy, toss ideas here, follow-ups at bottom.

Attendees (quick): Derek, Priya, Ethan, Maya, Liam (5m late), a couple people dialed in from SRE.

Topline status (one-liners):
- Routing: rolling deployment of bias-adjusted routing policy is in canary (PLAT-1423), observed slightly increased tail latency for model_small-quant on the canary hosts (p95 +18ms). Investigating batching behavior.
- Auth: token rotation dry-run succeeded in staging but we saw ~0.2% 401s from legacy clients — handshake mismatch; flagged for back-compat patch (PLAT-1478).
- Quotas: quota fallback simulation yesterday produced a high churn of fallthrough routes; need to tune cooldowns and backoff to avoid thrash.
- Controlplane: KV-cache warmup improvement PR ready (PR#612) — expect faster cold-starts for pinned models.

Detailed notes / observations:
1) Routing bias experiment (canary)
   - What happened: Canary route policy adds a cheap-model bias for low-cost traffic. The canary pool is using newer batcher config (dynamic weight), which produced slightly larger batches for short requests leading to queueing jitter.
   - Data: p50 unchanged; p95 +18ms; p99 marginal bump (~30ms). Token-level cost decreased by ~4% for canary traffic.
   - Hypothesis: dynamic-weight batcher increases aggregation window for model_small-quant because it tries to reach an efficiency target. On hosts with bursty short requests this causes small queue waits.
   - Mitigation options: reduce aggregation target for model_small-quant in the canary (quick), or apply per-model latency SLO overrides so batcher prioritizes latency for pinned models (longer).
   - Decision: Priya to toggle aggregation target to conservative on canary and rerun synthetic workload tomorrow (07/30). If p95 improves, proceed with staged rollout.

2) Auth token rotation follow-up
   - Dry-run in staging completed at 03:12 UTC; 401 spike traced to mobile clients that call /v1/verify with older TLS ciphers and do not properly refresh cached session blob.
   - Action: ETHAN to open a small compat shim in auth proxy to accept legacy blob for 7 days while we push client sdk fix. Ticket PLAT-1478 assigned.
   - Notes: Add an observability signal for token-kv-misses and correlate with client-version header (if present).

3) Quota fallback & throttling behavior
   - Simulation summary: when dedicated quota pool hits limit, we fallback traffic to shared pool. Short bursts cause oscillation where routes flip between pools frequently. Observed increase in quota-manager CPU due to constant resyncs.
   - Root cause: cooldown window currently 30s — too short for high-churn customers. Also routing decisions don't persist across controlplane leader restarts.
   - Proposed changes: (a) make cooldown adaptive (based on recent churn); (b) add a route affinity token persisted in KV store so restarts don't immediately flip decisions; (c) cap route flip rate per route (circuit-breaker).
   - Owners: Maya to prototype cooldown adaptive algo; Liam to spec route affinity token persistence (storage cost estimate first).

4) KV cache warmup PR (PR#612)
   - Summary: change is lazy-warmup at job startup using small parallel prefetch to avoid head-of-line blocking on first requests. Bench locally shows 30% improvement in cold-start p99 for model_medium.
   - Risk: additional memory during prefetch window; needs monitoring of jemalloc spikes.
   - Deployment plan: merge to canary after smoke tests; keep ramp gating at 10% for 24h; extra mem metrics on infra dashboard.

5) Observability gaps discovered
   - Missing spans between routing decision and quota check in the canary path. That makes latency attribution hard.
   - Quick fix: insert an explicit trace span in routing policy evaluator; longer term: align trace ids across pools.

Open questions / things to not forget:
- Should we prefer conservative latency-first even if cost increases slightly for customer tiers with strict SLOs? Need policy decision.
- How to quantify cost benefit of dynamic-batcher per workload without running long experiments? Can we simulate with traffic replayer?
- Backfills: update the runbook about quota fallback (runbook currently silent on persistent route affinity).

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya: toggle canary aggregation target and run synthetic workload (2026-07-30).
- Ethan: implement auth proxy compat shim and create rollout plan (2026-08-02).
- Maya: prototype adaptive cooldown algo and share bench notes (2026-08-06).
- Liam: spec route affinity token persistence and storage cost (2026-08-03).
- Derek: add trace span and create dashboard tile for routing->quota latency chain (2026-08-01).
- All: review PR#612 memory impact during next ops meeting (2026-08-04).

Notes to self (informal):
- Remember to mention that we saw a tiny regression in nightly job — correlate with upstream dependency bump (libbatcher v2.4.1)
- If we end up rolling back canary, have rollback tags ready and pre-announce to SRE on-call.

- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/612

- Runbook stub: confluence.redwood.com/pages/11429
- Slack thread: #pltfm-controlplane (thread ts: 1722000000.000300)

Wrap-up / next sync:
- Quick status check Friday 2026-07-31 10:00 PT to confirm canary toggles and auth shim staging results. If Priya reports green, start ramp to 30% canary.

End of braindump.

-- Derek
